items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: the same as Bill Johnson refused to talk to any contacts that I tried to make with him those last three or four years

ctx.x: Yeah. But they'd gone together... Anyway, say, 10 years or so ago, quite a while back. Anyway, George Barquet's brother, Sheil, who wasn't as well-known as George, down here at least, had passed for white for years. I know Mineta says he met him once on Canal Street after he started passing, and he said, well, I like it better. I forget. I have that in some of the Mineta interviews. Some of that stuff I'll copy, too, later on, which is on tape. He likes it better. Mineta sort of, you know, he wasn't mad at him or…

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-08-31
items.q: But in 1940 or 41, on the way back from California about that time, I stopped and saw him for the last time.

ctx.x: I don't suppose he would have any written material or pictures of anything like that?

No, he had good pictures at that time. I was hoping to get some of those pictures, which I didn't copy all of them. They had pictures of Big Eye, Louie, and people. I remember one in the boxing match of Big Eye and Freddie Keppert outside the theater. They had their fists up as if they were boxing. A few other good pictures, which I didn't, it cost too much to reproduce them, I guess, at the time. The Jazzman, I didn't see all of them at that time either. But in 1940 or 41, on the way back from California about…
This is a valuable document, isn't it? This document.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: He had quite a collection of pictures and I borrowed those and took them to New York.

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you how... I don't know whether... How did Ramsey and Smith... It says edited by Frederick Ramsey Jr. and Charles Edward Smith. Did they go through the whole book and decide which was going in and which was going left out?

No, that was all decided before. Actually, another funny thing was I don't even have my contract to prove it anymore. There were four editors, supposedly. Steve Smith and I were also listed as editors in the original contract and the idea was that we got a bigger... a bigger share of the advance or something by being an editor that way. We got more money to work with... I guess some of the others didn't even get $30 maybe. I don't know what the advance was. As I said, I don't even remember any details of the…
Now Ramsey was working for the Harcourt at this time.
